methods: The harrill screen used five hNP1 and four hN2 outputs, the existing vehicle standardization, the original five chemical folds, and five chemical-seeded contexts of three measured concentrations. AnchorBoost was refitted with its frozen 600-iteration recipe. The published conditional neural process (commit f9848800dfab66a8bc005e6b3087153eeaabe9ac) retained its source bytes and used the Gaussian interpolated configuration selected in published NFA folds 1–4, with the output dimension adapted to the screen. Three final-checkpoint models used seeds 0, 1 and 2, 4,000 steps each and batch size 32; their predicted means were averaged. No external test outcomes selected a configuration or checkpoint. MAE was averaged across observed concentration-level means, designs and chemical identities in that order. Paired percentile intervals used 10,000 chemical-identity resamples, seed 0. Both 95% and 97.5% intervals are supplied for the two-screen comparison. Method footnote: Valproate and Valproic Acid occur in different original folds; the identity-clean table excludes those two evaluation labels and retains all 71 original-label results separately. Absent hN2 measurements remain masked.
results: AnchorBoost yielded 2.83% lower MAE than the conditional neural process (1.694976 versus 1.744422; K−C -0.049446, 95% interval [-0.113124, +0.013459], 97.5% interval [-0.122864, +0.022714]; n=69 chemical identities). Chemical wins/losses/ties were 36/33/0; fold wins/losses/ties were 4/1/0.
